subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should unsupported Codex rollout mirror shapes be parsed into OpenClaw history, silently skipped as structured debug metadata, or replaced by a canonical OpenClaw transcript source for fallback and hooks?
rationale: The source supports several possible fixes with different ownership and compatibility tradeoffs, and automation cannot choose the permanent transcript/lifecycle contract for Codex app-server failover.

options.title: Use canonical OpenClaw transcript fallback
options.body: Route fallback and hook context through OpenClaw-owned transcript/session history when the Codex mirror is missing or has a Codex-only rollout shape, while preserving Codex thread ownership for normal continuity.

options.title: Parse Codex rollout history directly
options.body: Teach the mirror reader to understand Codex `session_meta` rollout files and materialize supported turn history, accepting a tighter dependency on Codex rollout internals.

options.title: Debug-skip unsupported mirrors only
options.body: Downgrade unsupported Codex mirror shapes to structured debug noise without changing fallback transcript semantics, leaving failover amnesia to a separate issue.

recommendation.title: Use canonical OpenClaw transcript fallback
recommendation.body: Route fallback and hook context through OpenClaw-owned transcript/session history when the Codex mirror is missing or has a Codex-only rollout shape, while preserving Codex thread ownership for normal continuity.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the recent partial fix and current blamed implementation around mirrored-history handling and shared-client cleanup.
